clue.text: Tree filmed in Hampshire

definitions.note: the definition names a place by its county, as a town found there

parts.note: the alder is a tree of damp ground
a scene that has been filmed has been shot

explanation.surface: A tree appears on camera somewhere in the south of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampshire is a county on England's south coast; ALDERSHOT is a garrison town in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The town is home to the British Army's base in that southern county.

clue.text: Appear as a weaver

definitions.meaning: to come into view, often ... large or threatening

explanation.definitionFit: To come into sight menacingly is one sense; the other is the frame on which yarn is woven into cloth.

clue.text: Little Edward passing out in a whirl

parts.note: Ed is a short form of the name Edward
passing out of life is dying

explanation.surface: Young Ed faints in a giddy spin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing out' suggests fainting, but here it means passing out of life.
explanation.definitionFit: Water swirling in circular currents is moving in a whirl.

clue.text: Most restful of tests in a way

indicators.note: in a way says the letters are arranged in some other fashion

explanation.surface: Some exams are more relaxing than others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a way' rearranges OF TESTS into SOFTEST.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentlest and quietest thing is the most restful.

clue.text: One who bosses the boss?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'One who bosses the boss?' has no count and pairs with 15-down 'See 5' to give OVERRULER, but the file holds OVER and RULER as separate unlinked entries, so neither light can be annotated on its own.

clue.text: How muggers inflict their cruelty

parts.note: describes the pitiless manner in which street robbers attack, without pity or guilt

explanation.definitionFit: Acting without pity or regret is acting without compunction.

clue.text: Place of business for the ruling class

definitions.meaning: a shop, firm or other business premises
the powerful group that controls society

explanation.definitionFit: A firm's premises is one sense; the other is the dominant elite holding power in a country.

clue.text: Empty-headed and quite illogical

explanation.definitionFit: A brainless person lacks common sense, and an absurd argument lacks meaning entirely.

clue.text: Cried because the car wouldn't go

explanation.definitionFit: Losing control and weeping is one sense; a vehicle suffering a mechanical failure is the other.

clue.text: Quiet dweller in high office

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
a resident is one who dwells in a place

explanation.surface: A silent inhabitant of a lofty government post.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a republic holds the top office of state.

clue.text: Cheat on board

definitions.meaning: a chess piece, the castle, found on the board

explanation.definitionFit: To swindle someone is one sense; the other is the castle among the chessmen.

clue.text: Rash complaint apiarists cope with

definitions.meaning: urticaria, a skin condition causing an itchy rash
beekeepers tend the structures their bees live in

explanation.definitionFit: Urticaria is an itchy skin condition; beekeepers tend the boxes where colonies live.

clue.text: Entertainment I find in remote surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings tells us one word encloses the other, the letter going within the word for remote

parts.note: a remote place is far away

explanation.surface: Amusement found in a distant setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A funfair with rides and stalls is a form of public amusement.

clue.text: One ably fitted for the country

indicators.note: fitted suggests the letters are put together in a new arrangement

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A capable person suited to their nation.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a North African nation on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: See 5

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'See 5' points to 5-down, giving OVERRULER, but the file holds the two lights as separate unlinked entries, so this one has no clue of its own to annotate.

clue.text: Endearing act of an un hesitant former U.S. statesman

indicators.note: without hesitation means the sound of hesitating, er, is dropped from the name

parts.note: Henry Kissinger was US Secretary of State

explanation.surface: A tender gesture by a confident retired American diplomat.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the written sound of hesitation, so 'un hesitant' removes it from KISSINGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiss is an affectionate gesture, so the act of doing it is endearing.

clue.text: Makes a mess of a hair-do?

definitions.text: Makes a mess of a hair-do?

parts.words: Makes a mess of a hair-do?
parts.note: describes ruffling someone's styled hair into disorder

explanation.definitionFit: To ruffle and dishevel is exactly what spoils a careful hairstyle.

clue.text: Indeed a song slowed up

indicators.note: In placed before the word tells us to put the next piece inside it

parts.note: taken as written
a lay is an old word for a song or ballad

explanation.surface: Indeed, a tune was played more slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: The single word 'Indeed' does two things: its first two letters are the container signal 'In', and the rest is the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held up or made late has been slowed.

clue.text: Count on him being a bloodsucker

definitions.text: Count on him being a bloodsucker

parts.words: Count on him being a bloodsucker
parts.note: reads as relying on someone being a leech, but describes the vampire count of Bram Stoker's novel

explanation.definitionFit: Bram Stoker's vampire is a Transylvanian nobleman who drinks blood.

clue.text: Confounded possibly, but not so much in a place of rest

indicators.note: in tells us the phrase for a smaller amount sits within the resting place

parts.note: a bed is where one rests
not so much means less

explanation.surface: Muddled, perhaps, but calmer somewhere quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. 'Blessed' works as a mild oath standing for 'confounded' or 'damned', as in 'the blessed thing won't start'.
explanation.definitionFit: As a mild curse ('the blessed thing!') it serves as a euphemism like damned.

clue.text: Comb manufacturer and autocrat join great conductor

parts.note: bees make honeycomb
a cham is an old form of khan, an absolute ruler

explanation.surface: A hair-comb maker and a dictator team up with a famous maestro.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comb' suggests a hair comb, but it is the honeycomb. Sir Thomas Beecham was a celebrated English conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Thomas, founder of the Royal Philharmonic, was a renowned English orchestral maestro.

clue.text: Proved to be hard to launder

parts.note: turned out to be, was
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Cleaning turned out to be difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: Laundering clothes means cleaning them with water and soap.

clue.text: Dead right subsequently

parts.note: the late person is one who has died

explanation.definitionFit: Something done afterwards happens at a following time.

clue.text: Conclude name is wrong: so be it

indicators.note: is wrong tells us the letters of the word are out of their proper order

explanation.surface: Decide the name is mistaken, and accept it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is wrong' rearranges NAME. 'Conclude' hints that the word closes a prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hebrew word said at the close of a prayer means let it be so.

clue.text: Fellow with a halo in South West Asia…

parts.note: a halo is a ring, shaped like the letter O
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A saintly man somewhere in the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: The ring-shaped halo is read as the letter O, placed before MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The sultanate lies on the south-east of the Arabian Peninsula.

clue.text: … about to lament

annotationWithheld.why: Clue '… about to lament' continues 24-down: its wordplay works on the words of the previous clue (Fellow with a halo, MAN around O), which cannot be quoted from this clue.

clue.text: Provide feature on healthy approach to port

parts.note: to ply someone with food is to provide it
the mouth is a facial feature
sound means healthy, as in sound in body

explanation.surface: Give a healthy-looking feature, on the way into the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Plymouth Sound is the bay leading into the naval port of Plymouth in Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: The bay is the stretch of water ships cross on their way into the Devon harbour.

clue.text: Hymn Nora and I render melodiously

indicators.note: render means to make or turn into something new, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Nora and I perform a hymn tunefully.
explanation.definitionFit: Singing together tunefully means singing in agreement of pitch.
